description: UMRCP implements multiple guidance laws for missile steering, including Proportional Navigation (PN), Augmented Proportional Navigation (APN), Pure Pursuit, and Command guidance. The PN implementation is the most interesting - it is the same fundamental equation used in real radar-guided missiles.

text: Proportional Navigation works on a simple principle: steer the missile perpendicular to the line-of-sight (LOS) to the target, with an acceleration proportional to both the closing velocity and the rate at which the LOS angle is rotating. The equation is a = N * Vc * LOS_rate, where N is the navigation constant (typically 3-5), Vc is the closing velocity, and LOS_rate is the angular rotation rate of the line from missile to target.

The intuition is: if the LOS angle is not changing, the missile is on a collision course and no correction is needed. If the angle is rotating, the target is moving off the collision path and the missile needs to steer harder. The faster you are closing and the faster the angle is changing, the harder you steer.

codeSnippet.name: proportional_nav.py - compute()
codeSnippet.data:
class ProportionalNavigation(GuidanceLaw):
    def __init__(self, nav_gain: float = 4.0):
        self.nav_gain = nav_gain
        self._prev_los_angle: float | None = None

    def compute(self, missile_pos: Vec2D, missile_vel: Vec2D,
                target_pos: Vec2D, target_vel: Vec2D, dt: float) -> Vec2D:
        rel_pos = target_pos - missile_pos
        rel_vel = target_vel - missile_vel

        los_angle = math.atan2(rel_pos.y, rel_pos.x)

        if self._prev_los_angle is None:
            self._prev_los_angle = los_angle
            return Vec2D(0.0, 0.0)

        # LOS rate: how fast the line-of-sight is rotating
        d_los = los_angle - self._prev_los_angle
        d_los = (d_los + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi  # Wrap to [-pi, pi]
        los_rate = d_los / dt if dt > 1e-9 else 0.0

        self._prev_los_angle = los_angle

        # Closing velocity (negative = closing)
        range_dist = rel_pos.magnitude()
        if range_dist < 1e-6:
            return Vec2D(0.0, 0.0)
        los_unit = rel_pos / range_dist
        closing_vel = -rel_vel.dot(los_unit)

        # a_cmd = N * Vc * LOS_rate, perpendicular to LOS
        accel_mag = self.nav_gain * closing_vel * los_rate

        perp = Vec2D(-math.sin(los_angle), math.cos(los_angle))
        return perp * accel_mag

text: The angle wrapping on line 18 ((d_los + pi) % (2*pi) - pi) is critical. Without it, when the LOS angle crosses the +/-pi boundary (target passes directly behind the missile), the computed rate spikes to an enormous value and the missile makes a wild correction. The wrapping normalizes the delta to always be the shortest angular path, preventing discontinuities.

list: Proportional Navigation - steers proportional to LOS rate, optimal against constant-velocity targets
Augmented PN - adds target acceleration compensation, better against maneuvering targets
Pure Pursuit - always points directly at the target, simple but inefficient (produces curved paths)
Command - steered externally by the radar, missile has no autonomy

text: Each guidance law implements the same GuidanceLaw interface with a compute() method, making them interchangeable in the simulation. Missiles can switch guidance laws mid-flight during failover - for example, switching from Command (radar-steered) to PN (autonomous) when their radar is destroyed.
